title: - What binds the world? By subduing what is one freed? By abandoning what thing Are all bonds destroyed? - Wish binds the world, By…
content:
- What binds the world?
By subduing what is one freed?
By abandoning what thing
Are all bonds destroyed?
- Wish binds the world,
By subduing sensual desire one is freed,
By abandoning wish,
All fetters are destroyed.

title: “To what extent, Venerable Gotama, is the Dhamma visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise?” -…
content: “To what extent, Venerable Gotama, is the Dhamma visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise?” - “Brahmin, being infatuated by craving, overwhelmed, with mind obsessed, one plans for one’s own harm, plans for others’ harm, plans for the harm of both, and experiences mental suffering and mental distress. When craving is abandoned, one does not plan for one’s own harm, nor for others’ harm, nor for the harm of both, and does not experience mental suffering or mental distress. Being infatuated by craving, brahmin, overwhelmed, with mind obsessed, one engages in misconduct of body, misconduct of speech, misconduct of mind. When craving is abandoned, one does not engage in misconduct of body, speech, or mind. Being infatuated by craving, brahmin, overwhelmed, with mind obsessed, one does not know as it actually is one’s own benefit, nor the benefit of others, nor the benefit of both. When craving is abandoned, one knows as it actually is one’s own benefit, the benefit of others, and the benefit of both. Thus, brahmin, the Dhamma is visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise.”

title: “And what, monks, is the origination of the world? Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With…
content: “And what, monks, is the origination of the world? Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With contact as condition, feeling. With feeling as condition, craving. With craving as condition, clinging. With clinging as condition, existence. With existence as condition, birth. With birth as condition, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. This is the origination of the world. Dependent on the ear … on the nose … on the tongue … on the body … Dependent on the mind and phenomena, mind-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With contact as condition, feeling. With feeling as condition, craving. With craving as condition, clinging. With clinging as condition, existence. With existence as condition, birth. With birth as condition, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. This, monks, is the origination of the world.”

title: “One who finds no core among becomings, Like one picking flowers from a fig tree — That monk abandons the near and far shore, Like…
content:
“One who finds no core among becomings,
Like one picking flowers from a fig tree —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

“One in whom there is no anger inside,
Who has gone beyond existence and non-existence —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

“One whose thoughts have been dispersed,
Internally well-ordered, without remainder —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

title: “One who restrains evil intent, Seeing the beautiful with sharp desire — That person’s craving increases; He makes the fetter strong.” “One who delights in…
content:
“One who restrains evil intent,
Seeing the beautiful with sharp desire —
That person’s craving increases;
He makes the fetter strong.”

“One who delights in calming the mind,
Always contemplating foulness, mindful —
That person will destroy craving;
He cuts off Māra’s fetter.”

“One who has reached the goal, without fear,
Free from craving, without defilement,
Having pulled out the dart of existence —
This body is his last.”

title: Greed, hatred, delusion — these three, Are evil minds for a person, They damage one’s own self, They produce one’s own self, Like the rind…
content:
Greed, hatred, delusion — these three,
Are evil minds for a person,
They damage one’s own self,
They produce one’s own self,
Like the rind and core of a tree,
Producing its own fruit.

title: “Monks, sensual thought is blind, causes blindness, causes lack of knowledge, leads to the destruction of wisdom, partakes of distress, does not lead to Nibbāna.…
content:
“Monks, sensual thought is blind, causes blindness, causes lack of knowledge, leads to the destruction of wisdom, partakes of distress, does not lead to Nibbāna. Monks, ill-will thought is blind … harmful thought is blind, causes blindness, causes lack of knowledge, leads to the destruction of wisdom, partakes of distress, does not lead to Nibbāna.

Three thoughts of wholesome kind
One should frequently reflect upon —
Three unwholesome thoughts should be abandoned, turned away from.
That one surely restrains
The conduct of thoughts.

As rain settles the dust,
So by calming thoughts with the mind,
One here and now attains
The peaceful path of peace.”

title: “Rāhula, develop the meditation on foulness. Rāhula, by developing the meditation on foulness, what is called lust is abandoned. Rāhula, develop the meditation on impermanence.…
content: “Rāhula, develop the meditation on foulness. Rāhula, by developing the meditation on foulness, what is called lust is abandoned. Rāhula, develop the meditation on impermanence. Rāhula, by developing the meditation on impermanence, what is called the conceit ‘I am’ is abandoned.”

title: “Monks, I will teach about suffering and the root of suffering. Listen … And what, monks, is suffering? Form, monks, is suffering; feeling is suffering;…
content: “Monks, I will teach about suffering and the root of suffering. Listen … And what, monks, is suffering? Form, monks, is suffering; feeling is suffering; perception is suffering; formations are suffering; consciousness is suffering. This, monks, is called suffering. And what, monks, is the root of suffering? It is this craving that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, delighting here and there — that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence.”

title: “And what, monks, is the peril in the case of feelings? Feelings are impermanent, suffering, subject to change – that is the peril in the…
content: “And what, monks, is the peril in the case of feelings? Feelings are impermanent, suffering, subject to change – that is the peril in the case of feelings. And what, monks, is the escape in the case of feelings? The removal of desire and lust for feelings, the abandoning of desire and lust – that is the escape in the case of feelings.”
